text:
maria: quick question — we saw three host_high_cpu alerts fire in us-west yesterday at ~03:10 but nobody paged. where are those alerts currently routed?
kevin: most host_high_cpu alerts are routed through the 'infra-hosts' PD service, which goes to eng-infra schedule by default. do you have the alert rule name/labels?
maria: alert rule is host_high_cpu (prometheus) with labels: severity=page, team=storage, env=prod, host_group=db-us-west. I expected it to go to the primary oncall for storage, not infra.
jon: sounds like the alerting rule might be using a generic pd_service label. we recently changed a few rules to point at infra to reduce noisy paging. could be side effect.
pd-bot: PagerDuty: Service "infra-hosts" (svc_ABC123) — Escalation policy: infra-escalation (2 levels) — Current on-call: kevin (weekdays) / sam (weekends) — Link: https://redwood.pagerduty.com/services/svc_ABC123
maria: ahhh ok. can we change routing for host_group=db-us-west to page storage oncall instead? storage owns the DB cluster. cc @sam in case weekend schedule matters.
kevin: yes. two options: 1) update the prometheus alert rule to set pd_service: svc_STORAGE456 for that host_group (preferred), or 2) add a routing rule in PD (service-level) to forward alerts matching metadata to storage service. I'd prefer option 1 so teams own their alerts.
kevin: sample of the alert rule change (place in prometheus/alerts/db.yaml):
```yaml
- alert: HostHighCPU
  expr: node_cpu_seconds_total{mode!="idle"} > 0.9
  labels:
    severity: page
    team: storage
    pd_service: "svc_STORAGE456"  # change from svc_ABC123
  annotations:
    summary: "High CPU on {{ $labels.instance }}"
```
kevin: after that, run `make deploy-alerts` in infra/alerting repo, and PD will start paginating storage oncall. also update the runbook note.
maria: where should I look to confirm the mapping quickly (logs/metrics/traces) while we make the change?
jon: for metrics/alerts: Grafana dash "Infra / Hosts -> db-us-west" — https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/hosts/db-us-west (open in VPN). for alert history: Alertmanager UI: https://alertmanager.redwood.internal/#/alerts. for traces: Tempo link on the Grafana panel / or Jaeger: https://traces.redwood.internal/search?service=db
sam: I can do the PD-side change if we want fast fix. but we should push the prometheus change so it's source of truth. I'll make a quick PD rule to forward matching alerts to storage for now.
kevin: if you do PD forwarding, remember to add a filter on metadata -> host_group=db-us-west and set urgency to high so it actually pages. PD forwarding without urgency=high might suppress.
sam: on it. will add forwarding rule + note in the change. ping me when you create the PR so I can revert the PD hack after deploy.
maria: thanks — created PR #812 in infra/alerting: https://git.redwood.internal/infra/alerting/pulls/812 — small yaml change, tests pass. please review when you get a sec @kevin @jon.
kevin: ack, will review in ~30m. also adding a little checklist to oncall runbook: where to check mappings (Alertmanager -> PD -> Grafana) and exec steps to fix routing quickly.
maria: perfect. also can we add a short note to oncall channel with `/pd who` command for quick reference? makes bootstrapping faster.
jon: good call. example: `/pd who --service svc_STORAGE456` shows current oncall. i'll add that to runbook too.
pd-bot: PagerDuty note: If you need PD help, tag @oncall-support or open an incident in PD.
maria: thanks everyone :thumbsup:
